value: A representative recommends a complex note that suits some investors to a small charity whose account needs ready cash and cannot bear losses. Which suitability obligation is breached?
reason: Rule 2111 no longer applies to recommendations covered by Reg BI (2020); a charity is not a natural person, so the suitability rule still governs.

value: A charity is not a natural person, so Reg BI does not apply and Rule 2111 does; customer-specific suitability asks about the particular investor at issue.
reason: Explains why Rule 2111, not Reg BI, applies to this customer.

value: B is met if it suits some investors. C concerns the number of trades. D is about knowing facts, which the representative seems to know.
reason: Matches the rewritten front.

value: Each recommendation a representative makes for a small family company’s account suits it on its own, but he recommends 60 trades there in three months. Which suitability obligation is in question?
reason: Quantitative suitability under Rule 2111 no longer applies to retail customers (2020); a company account keeps the scenario under the suitability rule.

value: Quantitative suitability looks at the number of recommended transactions within a period. The account belongs to a company, not a natural person, so Rule 2111 applies rather than Reg BI.
reason: Explains why the suitability rule governs this account.

value: It looks at a series of recommendations together, not at any single trade. Since 2020 FINRA no longer has to prove that the firm controlled the account.
reason: 2020 amendment removed the control element (2020-06187).

value: Since 2020 Rule 2111 does not apply to recommendations covered by Reg BI, so for retail customers Reg BI’s four obligations govern.
reason: Tells the learner when each regime applies (2020-06187).

value: The greater of $1,000,000 (the statute’s figure, which the SEC raises yearly for inflation) or three times the profit gained or loss avoided.
reason: 17 CFR 201.1001(b): civil penalty maximums are adjusted annually for inflation.

value: A controlling person is liable only if it knew or recklessly disregarded the likely violation and failed to act, or knowingly or recklessly failed to keep the required policies. Under its penalty rules (Rule 201.1001(b)) the SEC adjusts its civil penalty maximums for inflation every year, so the dollar amount in force is higher than the statute’s.
reason: Adds the inflation adjustment the back now mentions.
Dollar maximum changes every year.

value: 2026-09-25 · statutory figure; the SEC raises it yearly for inflation
reason: Dollar maximum changes every year.

value: The Federal Reserve Board’s regulation of credit by brokers and dealers, whose rules govern cash accounts and margin accounts alike.
reason: Reg T covers margin accounts (12 CFR 220.4) as well as cash accounts (220.8).

value: The bulletin ties Reg T’s credit rules to buying in a cash account; the same regulation also sets margin-account rules, such as the 50 percent initial margin.
reason: Explains the wider scope.

value: Publication 559’s example of joint tenants with right of survivorship has the survivor acquire the dead owner’s interest and add its value to the survivor’s basis.
reason: Points to the p. 20 example that shows the survivor acquiring the interest.

value: With right of survivorship, the dead owner’s share passes to the surviving joint tenant; Publication 559 treats the survivor as acquiring it.
reason: Says why the survivor holds the property.

value: B and C are Rule 17a-3(a)(6) and (18) records, which Rule 17a-4 keeps for three years (FINRA Rule 4513 asks four for complaint records). D is wrong for the same reason.
reason: Reconciles with Rule 4513’s four-year period.

value: The short name is built from the words of the official title. Among much else, its section 352 requires financial institutions to have anti-money laundering programmes.
reason: Adds what the Act does, from the same FinCEN page.

value: FINRA’s governing provisions, separate from the Rules of FINRA and arranged in articles, such as Article III on who may associate with a member.
reason: Gives a concrete article and its subject (2021-13286).

value: Being a paid director of another company is an outside business activity under Rule 3270, which needs prior written notice. Once Rule 3290 takes effect, only investment-related outside activities will need notice.
reason: Rule 3290 narrows reportable activities (2026-19126).

value: B: Rule 3270, still in force, covers business activity outside the firm, securities-related or not; Rule 3290 will narrow this once effective. C: Form U5 ends a registration; he is not leaving.
reason: Flags the coming change.

value: In 2010 FINRA gave no such exception for disclosures on Forms BD and U4, though it said it would work towards removing that duplicate reporting.
reason: Matches the notice’s "at this time".

value: Not accept the order: while CE inactive he may not perform, or be paid for, any activity requiring registration.
reason: Re-sourced to the 2021 notice; drops the trail-commission claim from the 2017 proposal.

value: Taking an order is an activity that requires registration, so he must leave it to a registered colleague who is not CE inactive.
reason: Explains the answer from the 2021 wording.

value: B: he may not perform any activity requiring registration, paid or not. C: inactivity covers all activities requiring registration, not only supervision.
reason: Matches the new source.

value: Federal Register doc. 2021-13286 (2021-06-24), SEC notice of proposed amendments to FINRA Rules 1210 and 1240, “Regulatory Element”
reason: Current wording of the CE inactive rule.

value: https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2021-06-24/html/2021-13286.htm
reason: Current wording of the CE inactive rule.

value: A CE inactive person is prohibited from performing, or being compensated for, any activities requiring FINRA registration, including supervision.
reason: Current wording of the CE inactive rule.

value: Until the 1 December 2026 compliance date, municipal advisors and bank dealers stay under the existing G-20 provisions; from that date the $300 limit applies to them too.
reason: Says what happens after the compliance date.
